title: ci(board-snapshot): upload only the records that changed to R2, not all ~41k objects every run
body:
## Why

The R2 step of `board-snapshot.yml` runs `aws s3 sync archive/board/ s3://$R2_BUCKET/objectstack/board/ --delete`. `aws s3 sync` uploads a file when its size differs from the object's, or when the local mtime is newer than the object's LastModified (aws-cli `SizeAndLastModifiedSync.compare_time`). A fresh CI checkout gives every file a brand-new mtime, so **every run re-PUTs all ~41,000 objects**. Measured on the `objectstack-board` bucket: 1.2M PutObject in 11 days (~110k a day at 4 runs a day). That is ~$10 a month of R2 Class A operations, against a free tier of 1M a month.

## What changes (`.github/workflows/board-snapshot.yml` only)

1. **Archive checkout:** `git fetch --depth=1` becomes `git fetch --filter=blob:none`. The archive branch's whole history is fetched without file contents. The worktree checkout still downloads the tip's blobs in one batch, the same content the depth-1 fetch downloaded, so the history adds only commits and trees: ~7 MB for 127 commits over 41,047 files, measured today with a blobless fetch of `board-archive`.
2. **R2 step:** before `aws s3 sync`, a short inline Node script sets each file's mtime to the committer time of the **last commit on the archive branch that changed it**. It uses one `git log --no-renames --name-only -z --format=%x01%ct HEAD -- board` pass over trees only (~0.2 s for today's history). The sync command itself is unchanged: same source, same `--delete`, same target.

Why that is correct:
- An object's LastModified is the time it was last uploaded. Every upload happens after the commit whose content it carries, because the commit step runs before the R2 step. So a current object's LastModified is newer than its file's restored mtime, and sync skips it.
- A file changed by a commit made after its object's last upload has the newer mtime and is uploaded. That covers this run's changes **and anything an earlier failed run did not upload**, with no state kept between runs.
- Files removed from the archive are still deleted by `--delete`.
- `--size-only` was rejected, as required: an `updated_at` move keeps a record's byte count.
- A truncated history (if `--depth` ever came back) only errs in the safe direction. The boundary commit looks like the creator of every older file, which stamps those files newer than their real change, so they are re-uploaded and no stale object is skipped.
- If the history cannot be read at all, the step leaves the checkout mtimes in place. That is the old full re-upload, announced in a `::warning::` and in the run's R2 status line. It costs more Class A operations and never gives a weaker copy.

Unchanged: the 4×/day schedule, the daily `snapshots/YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz` (its members now carry the restored mtimes), credentials read but never echoed, unset secrets as a notice, a configured upload that fails goes red, and the `--delete` target is never widened. Comments that the change made untrue were updated: the "every later run moves a handful" note was false before this PR and is true now. A new "Only changed records are uploaded" section documents the mechanism and its two assumptions:
- only this workflow writes the archive branch, so committer times follow real time;
- nothing else writes under the mirror prefix. An out-of-band same-size write with a newer LastModified would no longer be overwritten within six hours.

## Validation

The R2 step cannot run in a PR (skipped on `pull_request`). So I ran the **checkout, commit/push and R2 steps verbatim**, extracted from this workflow file, against a throwaway git server (`uploadpack.allowFilter`) and a fake `aws` that applies aws-cli's size+mtime rule to a JSON bucket and records content hashes. After every successful run it checks that the mirror equals the archive byte for byte:

| run | scenario | uploaded | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | old behaviour, fresh checkout | 60 of 60 | — |
| 1 | 2 edits (one same-size), 1 new, 1 deleted | exactly the 3 changed; 1 deleted | mirror == archive |
| 2 | upload fails | — | step red, as before |
| 3 | 1 more edit | run 2's 2 misses + its own 1 | mirror == archive |
| 4 | no change | 0 | mirror == archive |
| 5 | upload fails again | — | step red |
| 6 | **depth=1 history**, no change, R2 behind | 60 (over-upload, incl. run 5's miss) | mirror == archive |

The push from the blobless clone landed every run's commit on the server. **Ablation:** with the mtime restore replaced by `false` (one line), runs 1, 3 and 4 each upload all 60 objects and the harness reports 3 failures, so the test detects the old behaviour.

`actionlint` 1.7.12 with shellcheck 0.11.0 reports exactly the one finding untouched `main` already has (SC2086 on the intentionally unquoted `$SNAPSHOT_ARGS` in the snapshot step). The new script is clean. The repo's workflow-scanning gates were run locally on this branch and all exit 0: `check:pm-board-snapshot`, `check:pm-dispatch-gates`, `check:pm-expected-skips`, `check:node-version`, `check:pnpm-acquisition`, `check:workflow-step-name-quoting`, `check:workflow-status-functions`, `check:required-contexts`, `check:stall-guard-budget`, `check:shard-attestation`, `check:agent-test-spelling`, `check:pnpm-filter-targets`, `check-self-test-wired`, `check-step-collectors`, `check-whole-set-label-write`, `check-aggregator-roster` and `check-ci-filter-parity`.

## Expected effect

Per run: ~41,000 PutObject goes down to the records that changed since the last upload, plus the ~41 ListObjectsV2 pages sync already reads. The archive's last five commits touched 546 distinct files, so that is roughly a hundred per run, or ~13k a month against the 1M free tier. The first run after merge should log `mtimes from history: <n> file(s) stamped from <m> commit(s)` and a small `synced N object(s)`, which is the post-merge check.

## Notes

- Searched the open issues and PRs for this (`board-snapshot R2`, `s3 sync`) and found nothing. Earlier R2-mirror fixes in this file: #18049, #19536.
- Releases nothing from any published package, so `skip-changeset`.
